mainTopic: Bald spots and their size, removing hair on שבת, rounding the head and beard, and cutting the skin over the dead
overview: The גמרא first asks how someone can get separate lashes for five bald spots if he was warned only once, since a נזיר who keeps drinking after one warning gets only one set of lashes. It answers that the five spots were made at the same instant, with five fingers dipped in hair-removing cream, so the one warning covers each spot. Next it asks how big a forbidden קרחה must be. The views are the size of a גריס, big enough to be seen, two hairs, or a lentil, with a memory aid from the laws of נגעים. A ברייתא teaches that removing a scissorsful of hair on שבת makes one liable, and רב יהודה says that is two hairs. רבי אליעזר says one hair is enough, and everyone agrees one hair counts when a person picks white hairs out from black ones, which a man may not do even on a weekday. The גמרא then defines rounding the פאת הראש and discusses whether the person being rounded also gets מלקות. It also defines the פאת הזקן. Finally, a ברייתא learns from the פסוק that שריטה is forbidden only over the dead, and that each cut is counted separately. רבי יוסי counts each dead person through the word לנפש, and the גמרא challenges him because that word was already used. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Can one warning make him liable for five bald spots?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that one התראה could make someone liable for each of five bald spots, using a משנה about a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if there was only one warning, is he really liable for each one? But we learned: a נזיר who drank wine all day is liable only once. If people kept telling him 'Don't drink, don't drink' and he kept drinking, he is liable for each and every drink!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is checking how the משנה's case of five separate bald spots could work if there was only one warning. It brings a משנה about a נזיר to show that one warning normally gives only one set of lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said that if there were five warnings, the rule would be too obvious to teach. So now it tries one warning, but the נזיר case shows that many acts after a single warning count as one punishment. Each separate set of lashes needs its own warning.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning given right before a sin; it is needed before בית דין can give lashes
A person who took a vow to avoid wine, haircuts and contact with the dead
Is he really liable? (a doubting question)
Liable for each and every one separately

phrases.english: Rather, with one warning, is he liable?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: נָזִיר שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹתֶה יַיִן כׇּל הַיּוֹם –
phrases.english: But didn't we learn: A nazir who was drinking wine all day
is liable only once.
If they said to him: 'Do not drink,' 'Do not drink,'

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא שׁוֹתֶה – חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת!
phrases.english: and he drinks, he is liable for each and every one!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בַּחֲדָא הַתְרָאָה, מִי מִחַיַּיב? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier search for a case where the משנה's ruling of separate liability is not obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that one warning could cover five bald spots made one after another
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The נזיר משנה shows that repeated acts after one warning bring only one punishment.

steps.title: Five fingers with hair-removing cream at once
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where he put cream on five fingers and pressed them on his head all at the same moment, so the single warning applies to every spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where he smeared his five fingers with hair-removing cream and placed them all at once. Then it counts as a warning for each and every spot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by describing a special case: five bald spots made in one single motion right after one warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נזיר drank at different times, so one warning covered only the first drink. Here all five spots happen at the very same moment, so the one warning applies equally to each spot. The new point is that each spot is still its own separate sin.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case
A hair-removing cream or paste
All at once, at the same moment

steps.whatToRemember: Five bald spots made at the same instant after one warning bring five sets of lashes, because each spot is a separate sin.

phrases.aramaic: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּסָךְ חֲמֵשׁ אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו נָשָׁא
phrases.english: No, it is necessary where he smeared his five fingers with depilatory cream
and placed them all at once,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָוְיָא לֵיהּ, הַתְרָאָה לְכׇל חֲדָא וַחֲדָא.
phrases.english: so that it is for him a warning for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּסָךְ חֲמֵשׁ אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו נָשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the נזיר משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Five spots after one warning would seem to bring only one punishment, like the נזיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: When all five spots are made at the same instant, the one warning covers each, and he is liable five times.

steps.title: How big must a bald spot be?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the minimum size of a forbidden קרחה is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how big is the measure of a bald spot?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: how big a bald spot must be before one gets lashes. This question sets up the opinions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lashes need a clear minimum amount. Removing a few hairs may not count as a קרחה at all, so the גמרא needs a שיעור.

keyTerms.meaning: Minimum measure or amount
A bald spot made on the head in mourning for the dead, which the תורה forbids

phrases.english: And how much is the measure of a bald spot?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the same prohibition of קרחה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum size of a bald spot that brings liability.

steps.title: רב הונא and רבי יוחנן disagree on the size
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the spot must be big enough to be seen on the head. רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, says the size of a גריס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא says: enough that it can be seen on his head. רבי יוחנן says in the name of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: the size of a גריס bean.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different answers to the size question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא uses a visible test: the bald patch has to show. רבי יוחנן gives a fixed measure, a גריס, which is a kind of bean.

keyTerms.meaning: The size of a גריס, a type of bean
Enough that it shows on his head

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא אוֹמֵר: כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּרָאֶה מֵרֹאשׁוֹ.
phrases.english: Rav Huna says: Enough that it will be seen on his head.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon:
The size of a bean.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא אוֹמֵר: כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּרָאֶה מֵרֹאשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the size question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two opinions: visible on the head (רב הונא) or the size of a גריס (רבי יוחנן).

steps.title: The same argument among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the argument of the אמוראים matches an earlier argument between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like an argument of תנאים: How big is a bald spot? The size of a גריס. אחרים say: enough that it shows on his head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the two opinions already appear in a ברייתא as an argument among תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The unnamed first opinion matches רבי יוחנן's גריס, and אחרים match רב הונא. So each אמורא is following an earlier תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: This matches an argument among the תנאים
'Others', an unnamed group of תנאים quoted in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It is like a dispute of tannaim: How much is the measure of a bald spot? The size of a bean.
Acherim say: Enough that it will be seen on his head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the argument of the אמוראים to an earlier argument of תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גריס view and the 'visible' view are both earlier opinions of תנאים.

steps.title: Three תנאים disagree, with a third view of two hairs
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר חביבא reports that three תנאים disagree: a גריס, visible on the head, or two hairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר חביבא said: three תנאים disagree about this. One says a גריס, one says enough to show on his head, and one says two hairs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה בר חביבא adds a third opinion to the argument: just two hairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this we had only two views. Now there is a much smaller third measure, two hairs, which would make even very little hair removal punishable.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree
Three תנאים
Two hairs

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Chaviva said:
Three tannaim disagree about it.
One says: The size of a bean.
And one says: Enough that it will be seen on his head.
And one says: Like two hairs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר חֲבִיבָא: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ תְּלָתָא תַּנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the two-way argument into a three-way argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three views: a גריס, visible on the head, or two hairs.

steps.title: Another version replaces two hairs with a lentil
steps.stepSummary: Some take out the 'two hairs' opinion and put in its place an opinion of the size of a lentil.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there is someone who removes 'two hairs' and puts in 'like a lentil.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a different version of רב יהודה בר חביבא's list, where the third opinion is a lentil instead of two hairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version all three opinions are about the area of the bald patch: a גריס, a lentil, or enough to be seen. None of them counts single hairs.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes out, removes
Puts in, inserts
The size of a lentil

phrases.english: And there is one who takes out 'two hairs'
and puts in 'like a lentil.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּמַפֵּיק שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת וּמְעַיֵּיל בְּכַעֲדָשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of the third opinion in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In another version, the third view is a lentil, not two hairs.

steps.title: A memory aid from the laws of נגעים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן for remembering the גריס and lentil sizes: a בהרת is a גריס and מחיה is a lentil.
steps.simpleTranslation: And your memory aid: a בהרת is the size of a גריס, and מחיה is the size of a lentil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a memory trick so the learner remembers the two measures, the גריס and the lentil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the laws of צרעת, the white mark called a בהרת is a גריס, and the healthy-looking raw flesh inside it, called מחיה, is a lentil. These well-known measures help one remember the same two measures for קרחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Your memory aid
A bright white mark of צרעת
Raw, healthy-looking flesh inside a צרעת mark

phrases.english: And your mnemonic: A white leprous mark is the size of a bean,
and raw flesh is the size of a lentil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a memory aid for the measures just listed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Remember the גריס and lentil measures through בהרת and מחיה.

steps.title: Removing a scissorsful of hair on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that someone who removes a 'scissorsful' of hair on שבת is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: someone who removes a scissorsful of hair on שבת is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ברייתא about removing hair on שבת. It sets up a question about how much a 'scissorsful' is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting hair is one of the forbidden מלאכות of שבת, and it too needs a minimum amount. The ברייתא gives that amount as 'a scissorsful' but does not say how many hairs that is.

keyTerms.meaning: A scissorsful, as much hair as the blades of scissors grab at once
One who removes or takes off
The day of rest, when cutting hair is a forbidden מלאכה

phrases.english: It was taught: One who removes a scissorsful
on Shabbat is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הַנּוֹטֵל מְלֹא פִּי הַזּוּג בַּשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related source about a minimum amount of hair removal, this time for שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Removing a scissorsful of hair on שבת brings liability.

steps.title: How much is a scissorsful?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what amount 'a scissorsful' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is a scissorsful?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact meaning of 'a scissorsful.' This sets up רב יהודה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase is not clear: it could mean a large clump or just a few hairs. A clear number is needed to know when one is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much?

phrases.english: And how much is a scissorsful?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the ברייתא's measure.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The number of hairs in 'a scissorsful.'

steps.title: רב יהודה: two hairs
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says a scissorsful is two hairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: two.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers that a scissorsful means just two hairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vague phrase 'a scissorsful' is given an exact number: two hairs. So removing even two hairs on שבת makes one liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Two, meaning two hairs

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: Two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the scissorsful.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists two hairs for קרחה separately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה from a ברייתא that says 'for קרחה, two,' which sounds like the two-hair rule is only for קרחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: for a bald spot, two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה with a ברייתא that gives 'two' as the measure for קרחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'for קרחה, two,' naming קרחה specifically. That sounds like two hairs is special to קרחה, so the שבת measure must be different. This goes against רב יהודה, who said a scissorsful on שבת is two.

keyTerms.meaning: For a bald spot

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: For a bald spot, two!
phrases.notes: The challenge is that if two hairs is singled out for קרחה, then שבת must have a different measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's view that a scissorsful on שבת is two hairs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Listing 'two' for קרחה separately suggests that the שבת measure is not two.

steps.title: Read it as 'and likewise for קרחה, two'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the reading of the ברייתא: 'and likewise for קרחה, two,' so שבת and קרחה have the same measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: and likewise for a bald spot, two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing the wording of the ברייתא so it agrees with רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By adding the word 'likewise,' the ברייתא no longer sets קרחה apart from שבת. Now it says both have the same measure, two hairs, which fits רב יהודה exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead, read the text this way
And likewise, the same applies

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יהודה, removing two hairs on שבת brings liability, and the same two-hair measure applies to קרחה.

phrases.english: Say: And likewise for a bald spot, two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say two hairs is only the measure for קרחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means שבת and קרחה share the same measure of two hairs.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the two-hair measure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that clearly says a scissorsful on שבת is two hairs, backing up רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: one who removes a scissorsful of hair on שבת is liable. How much is a scissorsful? Two hairs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as proof that רב יהודה was right: a scissorsful means two hairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said a scissorsful is two hairs, and the גמרא just defended him from a challenge. Now it shows a ברייתא that says the same thing word for word, so his number is confirmed.

keyTerms.meaning: Also like this, a source that matches what was just said
A scissorsful, the amount of hair a pair of scissors takes in one cut
Liable, he has broken the law and is responsible for it

phrases.english: It is also taught like this:

phrases.aramaic: הַנּוֹטֵל מְלֹא פִּי הַזּוּג בַּשַּׁבָּת חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: One who removes a scissorsful of hair on Shabbat is liable,
and how much is a scissorsful? Two hairs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms רב יהודה's measure, which was just defended in step 13
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's rule that a scissorsful is two hairs
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says outright that a scissorsful is two

steps.title: One hair is enough for רבי אליעזר, and the חכמים agree when picking white hairs
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that one hair makes a person liable. The חכמים agree with him when someone picks white hairs out from among black ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: one hair. And the חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר that one who picks white hairs out from among black ones is liable even for a single hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא goes on: רבי אליעזר disagrees and says one hair is enough. In one case, picking out white hairs, the חכמים agree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the חכמים need two hairs before he is liable. But a person picking out white hairs wants each hair he pulls, so even one finishes the job he set out to do, and the חכמים agree he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים agree, here only in this one case
Picks out, removing chosen hairs one at a time
White hairs from among the black ones

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not dropping their two-hair rule. They agree to one hair only in the special case of picking white hairs from black.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: One hair.
And the Rabbis agree with Rabbi Eliezer
about one who picks out white hairs from among black ones,
that even for one hair he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a dissenting view and a case where everyone agrees
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי אליעזר, one hair makes a person liable. When someone picks white hairs from black ones, everyone agrees one hair is enough.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אַחַת. וּמוֹדִים חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר

steps.title: A man may not pick out white hairs even on a weekday
steps.stepSummary: Picking white hairs from black ones is forbidden for a man even on a regular weekday, because of the פסוק 'a man shall not wear a woman's garment.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is forbidden even on a weekday, because it says: 'A man shall not wear a woman's garment.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds that picking out white hairs is not only a שבת problem. A man may not do it on any day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a separate איסור from שבת. Picking out white hairs to look nicer is something women do, so for a man it falls under the איסור of dressing or grooming like a woman.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular weekday, not שבת or יום טוב
A man shall not wear a woman's garment, the איסור of acting or dressing like a woman

steps.whatToRemember: A scissorsful is two hairs. רבי אליעזר says one. Everyone agrees one hair is enough when picking white hairs, and a man may not do that even on a weekday.

phrases.english: And this thing is forbidden even on a weekday,
because it is said:
"A man shall not wear a woman's garment."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a weekday איסור to the case of picking white hairs
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man may not pick white hairs out from black ones even on a weekday, because of לא ילבש גבר שמלת אשה.

steps.title: Defining the 'edge of the head'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's case of rounding the פאת הראש. A ברייתא explains that it means making the temples even with the bare area behind the ear and the forehead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'one who rounds the edge of his head.' The חכמים taught: 'the edge of his head' means the end of his head. What is the end of his head? It is someone who makes his temples level with the area behind his ear and his forehead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה about rounding the פאת הראש and brings a ברייתא that explains exactly which area is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Behind the ears and on the forehead there is no hair. Someone who takes off the hair at the temples so the hairline runs straight across with those bare areas has 'rounded' his head.

keyTerms.meaning: One who rounds, removing hair so the hairline goes around evenly
The edge of his head, the hair at the temples
His temples
His forehead

phrases.english: The משנה said: And one who rounds the edge of his head, etc.
The Rabbis taught: "The edge of his head" means the end of his head,
and what is the end of his head?
This is one who makes his temples level
with the area behind his ear and with his forehead.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פְּאַת רֹאשׁוֹ – סוֹף רֹאשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rounding the פאת הראש means taking off the hair at the temples so they are level with the bare area behind the ear and the forehead.

steps.title: Both the one rounding and the one being rounded get מלקות
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites a ברייתא before רב חסדא: both the person who rounds and the person whose head is rounded get מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught in front of רב חסדא: both the one who rounds and the one who is rounded get lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא is brought that makes even the passive person, whose head is being rounded, get מלקות. This sets up רב חסדא's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is that the one being rounded also gets מלקות, not just the barber. That sounds strange, because he did nothing with his own hands.

keyTerms.meaning: The one being rounded, the person whose head someone else rounds
Gets lashes (מלקות)
Here, a person whose job was to memorize and recite ברייתות in the בית המדרש

phrases.english: A tanna taught in front of Rav Ḥisda:
Both the one who rounds and the one who is rounded get lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds who gets punished for the rounding that was just defined
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both the one who rounds and the one who is rounded get מלקות.

steps.title: Does someone who just sits there get lashes?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא objects: the person being rounded did nothing, like a man sitting and eating dates from a sieve. Why should he get מלקות?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: does a person who eats dates from a sieve get lashes?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא attacks the ברייתא with a sharp comparison. The person being rounded is passive, so how can he get מלקות?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally there are no מלקות for a לאו unless the person did an action. The one being rounded just sat there, as relaxed as someone snacking on dates, so the ברייתא seems wrong to punish him.

keyTerms.meaning: Dates (the fruit)
A sieve
Gets lashes (Aramaic form of לוקה)

phrases.english: He said to him: one who eats dates
from a sieve, does he get lashes?
phrases.notes: He means: the one being rounded did no more than a man sitting and snacking. Why punish him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 18 that the one being rounded gets מלקות
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that the הניקף gets מלקות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There are no מלקות for a לאו without an action, and the one being rounded did no action.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא tells the תנא: if someone asks who taught this ברייתא, answer that it is רבי יהודה, who gives מלקות even for a לאו with no action.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone asks you who taught this, say it is רבי יהודה, who holds that a לאו with no action still gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains how the ברייתא could still be right: it follows רבי יהודה's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that the passive person did no action. רבי יהודה holds that a לאו שאין בו מעשה still gets מלקות, so by his view the הניקף can be punished. The ברייתא is then a minority view and not everyone's opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? Asking which תנא is behind this teaching
A negative commandment that is broken without doing any action
One gets lashes for it

phrases.english: If someone says to you: Who taught this?
It is Rabbi Yehuda, who says:

phrases.aramaic: לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה לוֹקִין עָלָיו.
phrases.english: For a prohibition that has no action, one gets lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר לָךְ: מַנִּי – רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חסדא's own question by tying the ברייתא to one תנא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the ברייתא to a specific תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא looked like everyone's view, which would mean a passive person gets מלקות
steps.terutzMaskana: It is רבי יהודה, who gives מלקות even for a לאו without action

steps.title: Rounding his own head
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the ברייתא as a man rounding his own head. Then everyone agrees he gets מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: it is talking about one who rounds his own head, and everyone agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer so the ברייתא can fit everyone's opinion, not only רבי יהודה's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a man rounds his own head, he is both the one rounding and the one being rounded, and he certainly did an action. So he gets מלקות according to everyone, and the passive-person problem never comes up.

keyTerms.meaning: For himself, on his own head
Everyone's opinion, all agree

phrases.english: Rava says: it is about one who rounds his own head,
and it is everyone's opinion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another answer to רב חסדא's question, so the ברייתא need not depend on רבי יהודה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the ברייתא as a narrower case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'one who is rounded' seemed to be a passive person
steps.terutzMaskana: He rounded his own head, so he did an action, and everyone agrees he gets מלקות

steps.title: The one being rounded helped
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the one being rounded helped the barber, for example by moving his head. So everyone agrees he gets מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי says: it is talking about one who helps, and everyone agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third answer. The ברייתא is about someone whose head is rounded by another person, but who actively helped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבא, רב אשי keeps two different people. But the one being rounded helped, for instance by turning his head, and that counts as an action, so even those who disagree with רבי יהודה give him מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Helps, takes an active part in what is done to him

steps.whatToRemember: The one being rounded gets מלקות only if: we follow רבי יהודה (no action needed), or he rounded himself (רבא), or he helped the one rounding (רב אשי).

phrases.english: Rav Ashi says: it is about one who helps.
And it is everyone's opinion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to רב חסדא's question, parallel to רבא's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the ברייתא as a narrower case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The one being rounded seemed fully passive
steps.terutzMaskana: He helped the one rounding, which counts as an action, so everyone agrees he gets מלקות
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא can fit everyone's opinion when the one being rounded did some action himself.

steps.title: What counts as the 'edge of the beard'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about destroying פאת זקנו, and a ברייתא defines it as the end of the beard, its 'stalk.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And one who destroys the edge of his beard.' The Rabbis taught: the edge of his beard is the end of his beard. And what is the end of his beard? The 'stalk' of his beard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה and uses a ברייתא to explain which part of the beard פאת זקנו means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word פאה (edge) is defined as סוף, the end of the beard. That is then made exact: the שבולת, the spots where the hair gathers like grain on a stalk. This tells us which part of the beard the איסור is about.

keyTerms.meaning: Destroys, here meaning removing the beard hair
The edge of his beard
The end (outer part) of his beard
The 'stalk' of his beard, the spots where the hair gathers

phrases.english: "And one who destroys the edge of his beard."

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פְּאַת זְקָנוֹ – סוֹף זְקָנוֹ,
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: "The edge of his beard" means the end of his beard.
And what is the end of his beard?
The "stalk" of his beard.
phrases.notes: Literally 'ear of grain.' These are the spots where the beard hair bunches together like grain on a stalk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the discussion of rounding the head, the גמרא moves on to the next case in the משנה, the beard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פאת זקנו means the end of the beard, which is the שבולת, the spots where the hair gathers.

steps.title: Cutting the skin is forbidden only over a dead person
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the איסור of שריטה applies only to cutting over a dead person, not over a lost house or ship, because the פסוק says לנפש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And one who makes one cut, etc.' The Rabbis taught: 'And a cut.' I might think he is liable even if he cut himself over his house that fell or over his ship that sank in the sea. So the פסוק says 'for the soul': he is liable only over a dead person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה, cutting the skin in mourning, and brings a ברייתא that limits it to mourning for the dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק only said ושרט, we might think any cut made out of sadness is forbidden, even over lost property. The word לנפש ('for the soul') narrows it down: only cutting over a dead person brings מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: A cut in the skin, made as a sign of mourning
'I might think', introducing a mistaken idea the פסוק will correct
'The פסוק teaches', bringing the word in the פסוק that answers the question
'For the soul', meaning for a dead person

phrases.english: "And one who makes one cut, etc."
The Rabbis taught: "And a cut":

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ שָׂרַט עַל בֵּיתוֹ שֶׁנָּפַל
phrases.english: I might think: even if he cut himself over his house that fell down
or over his ship that sank in the sea?
So the פסוק says: "For the soul":

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא עַל הַמֵּת בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: he is liable only for cutting over a dead person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַמְשָׂרֵט שְׂרִיטָה אַחַת וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וְשֶׂרֶט״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא moves on to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שריטה brings מלקות only when it is done over a dead person, learned from the word לנפש.

steps.title: Five cuts for one dead person bring five punishments
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: someone who makes five cuts over one dead person is liable for each cut, learned from the word ושרט.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that someone who makes five cuts over one dead person is liable for each one? The פסוק says 'and a cut,' to make him liable for every single cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא now explains how we count the punishments when a person makes several cuts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know which kind of cut is forbidden (over the dead). This step adds a counting rule: each cut is its own עבירה. The word ושרט is read as 'every cut' and not just 'cutting in general.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where do we know?', asking for a source
Each and every one, counted separately

phrases.aramaic: וּמִנַּיִן לַמְשָׂרֵט חָמֵשׁ שְׂרִיטוֹת עַל מֵת אֶחָד
phrases.english: And from where do we know that one who makes five cuts over one dead person

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת?
phrases.english: is liable for each and every one?
The פסוק says: "And a cut":
to make him liable for each and every cut.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן לַמְשָׂרֵט חָמֵשׁ שְׂרִיטוֹת עַל מֵת אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, moving from which cut is forbidden to how the punishments are counted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Several cuts over one dead person bring a separate punishment for each cut.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: one cut for five dead people brings five punishments
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי teaches that one cut made for five dead people makes a person liable for each dead person, learned from לנפש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: From where do we know that someone who makes one cut over five dead people is liable for each one? The פסוק says 'for the soul,' to make him liable for every single soul.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי adds a second way of counting: by the number of dead people, not only by the number of cuts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא counted by cuts using ושרט. רבי יוסי counts by people using לנפש: 'every soul.' So a single cut can bring several punishments if it is made for several dead people.

keyTerms.meaning: Dead people
Each and every soul, meaning each dead person

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two words apart: ושרט counts the cuts, while לנפש (for רבי יוסי) counts the dead people.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן לַמְשָׂרֵט שְׂרִיטָה אַחַת
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: From where do we know that one who makes one cut
over five dead people

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת?
phrases.english: is liable for each and every one?
phrases.notes: Here 'each one' means each dead person, not each cut.

phrases.english: The פסוק says: "For the soul":
to make him liable for each and every soul.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן לַמְשָׂרֵט שְׂרִיטָה אַחַת עַל חֲמִשָּׁה מֵתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second counting rule to the ברייתא, using the word לנפש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, one cut over several dead people brings a separate punishment for each dead person.

steps.title: Wasn't לנפש already used for the house and the ship?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי: the word לנפש was already used to exclude cutting over a fallen house or a sunken ship, so how can it also teach counting by dead people?
steps.simpleTranslation: But you already used it to exclude his house that fell and his ship that sank in the sea!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוסי's source: one word seems to be doing two jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier part of the ברייתא, לנפש taught that the איסור is only over the dead and not over property. רבי יוסי now uses the same word to count each dead person. The question is how one word can teach both things. The גמרא answers this on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But surely', opening a challenge
'You took it out', meaning you already used the word to exclude something

phrases.english: But surely you already used it to exclude
phrases.notes: 'It' is the word לנפש, which step 24 used to rule out cutting over lost property.

phrases.english: his house that fell and his ship that sank in the sea!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אַפֵּיקְתֵּיהּ לְבֵיתוֹ שֶׁנָּפַל וְלִסְפִינָתוֹ שֶׁטָּבְעָה בַּיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוסי's source in step 26 because the same word was already used in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's use of לנפש to count each dead person
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One word in the פסוק cannot normally teach two different things. לנפש was already needed to exclude a fallen house and a sunken ship, so it seems it cannot also teach counting by dead people.
